status_note: TYPEFACTORY-DOWNCHAIN-VIRTUAL-0001 freezes the virtual downChain dispatch (plain type.cc:1084-1121 / relative type.cc:2656-2672) against locked Ghidra e40ed130 and Rugra production candidate f9307c7 (down_chain_virtual dispatcher plus the rel recover-parent accumulator fix, the rel tail no-fallback fix, and the plain par=this / wrap-zero return-this identity fix). The 25-record projection covers field hits, hole/null descents, off==0 and off==size boundaries, negative-encoded wrap, the enum branch, multi-level array chains with carried accumulators, rel-input re-propagation, and plain/rel routing discrimination. No production caller is wired in the candidate (B1 coreaction/typeop wiring is a follow-up lease), so no user-visible pipeline repair is claimed. getTypePointerStripArray's hasStripped pre-strip and calcTruncate are outside the covered input domain (no stripped field/element types, no alternate pointer size) and remain registered residuals under TYPE-0001/TYPEFACTORY-ARC-IDENTITY-0001 rather than being normalized.

architecture.spaces: const=0, other=1, unique=2, ram=3, register=4, stack=5, join=6, iop=7; all byte-addressed except the standard synthetic stack relationship
architecture.data_organization_input: explicit size/alignment entries 0:1,1:1,2:2,3:2,4:4,8:8,16:8,32:8; output alignment and aligned-width values are read from real Datatype objects and are not predeclared as oracle results
architecture.factory_bootstrap: Identical to the typefactory_exactpiece_1204 baseline: C++ TypeFactory(Architecture*) and Rust TypeFactory::raw(), with neither convenience core set installed; decode the identical data_organization; setupSizes/setup_sizes with stack-spacebase size 8, default data address size 8, default size 8, and no far pointer; parse the identical enum config; register exactly one named core type undefined1 size=1 TYPE_UNKNOWN unsigned=false; call cacheCoreTypes/cache_core_types; leave max_basetype_size at the shared default 10
architecture.factory_type_construction: Both sides obtain anonymous noncore uint4/uint8 with getBase/get_base_result; named structs Inner8{lo@0,hi@4}/Progress24{head@0,hole,inner@8,total@16}/Holed12{head@0,hole,tail@8}/Holder24{elems@0=Inner[3]} via the production composite setters with explicit size/alignment (8/4, 24/8, 12/4, 24/4); arrays Inner[3] and Inner[3][2]; enum8; plain pointers and four ephemeral PointerRel values (uint8+16@Progress, Inner+8@Progress, uint4+4@Holed, uint4+0@Progress) all through the corresponding production factory APIs. Names, sizes, offsets, alignments, call order, and shared object identities are held fixed by the 25-case manifest. Ghidra TypeField.ident has no Rust representation; the covered downChain closure never reads it (TYPEFIELD-IDENT-REPRESENTATION-0001 residual, identical to the exactpiece boundary).

compiler_spec.reason: This fixture calls TypeFactory directly and does not decode instructions or run an action pool. The complete compiler-spec-equivalent inputs consumed by setupSizes are the stack pointer size 8, default data-space address size 8, default size 8, no far-pointer segment, and the explicit data-organization/enum XML above.

host_toolchain.cargo_config_policy: reject config and config.toml in CARGO_HOME and every candidate working-directory ancestor, including the candidate root
host_toolchain.unfingerprinted_host_closure: The runner does not separately pin make, ar, the linker, libc/libstdc++, or kernel/filesystem behavior. It therefore makes no fully-hermetic build claim; the locked source/tool frontends and exact stdout hashes are the bounded behavior fingerprint.

analysis_options.entrypoints: Direct raw-factory bootstrap identical to typefactory_exactpiece_1204; target calls are the 25 virtual input->downChain(off,par,parOff,allowWrap,typegrp) invocations (Rugra: TypeFactory::down_chain_virtual). No instruction decode, Action, Rule, or decompiler pipeline is run.
analysis_options.type_graph: One shared raw factory owns anonymous noncore uint4/uint8; named inner8/progress24/holed12/holder24 structs with explicit holes; Inner[3] and Inner[3][2] arrays; enum8; seven plain pointers (progress/holed/array/array2/holder/uint4/enum, all size 8 wordsize 1); and four ephemeral PointerRel values from the unnamed parent-pointer overload. Only undefined1 is core.
analysis_options.normalization: No output-line or semantic-value normalization. The one representation encoding is the pointer shape projection: plain pointers render ptr:<size>-><shape(pointee)> and PointerRel render ptrrel:<size>-><kind:size of pointee>+<byte offset>@<kind:size of parent>; identity is emitted as C++ pointer equality / Rust Arc::ptr_eq bits, never as addresses. Accumulators start at par=NULL and parOff=-999 per record except chain_step2, which carries step1's off/par/parOff so the propagateAddIn2Out do-while accumulation is directly observable.
analysis_options.iteration_order: Twenty-five records in the fixed input_manifest order; chain_step1/chain_step2 run consecutively sharing accumulator state
analysis_options.api_domain: All offsets are int8-representable and within the int4 domain; every wrap flag and offset value is representable on both sides. Offsets outside int8, variable-length arrays, wordsize != 1 pointers, and spacebase pointees are deliberately UNTESTED rather than normalized.
analysis_options.production_caller_state: The fixture directly calls the frozen virtual dispatch entry on both sides. No production caller does: coreaction.rs:3970-3991 still propagates pointers untransformed and typeop.rs still lacks propagateAddIn2Out (upstream audit B1 items 1/4/9). This fixture therefore proves no production-consumer or user-visible pipeline repair; the progressbarinit PTRSUB wiring is the follow-up B1 lease.

input_manifest.canonicalization: SHA-256 of UTF-8 json.dumps(cases, sort_keys=true, separators=(',',':'), ensure_ascii=false)

cases.note: plain struct field hit: total uint8 field pointer, par=this, off renormalized to 0
nested struct field hit: Inner pointer via strip-array no-op
mid-field offset: head uint4 returned with remainder off_out=2
structure hole [4,8): getSubType NULL while par/parOff are still written
off==0 boundary: first-field pointer
off==alignSize with wrap denied: NULL before any off/par mutation
off==alignSize with wrap: sign_extend modulo folds to zero and returns this pointer
negative-encoded offset, wrap denied (PTRSUB style): NULL
negative-encoded wrap: -4 %% 24 + 24 = 20, parOff keeps pre-renormalized 20, off_out=4
array element descent: struct element preserved by getTypePointer, remainder 4
struct field of array type: non-array path strips one array layer off the component
array of arrays: array path keeps the Inner[3] element type intact
first propagateAddIn2Out-style do/while iteration: array level with fresh accumulators
second chain step: carried off/par/parOff, struct level overwrites par to itself
hole descent returning NULL with the container still recorded in par
scalar pointee: base getSubType NULL, accumulators untouched
scalar off==alignSize wrap: folds to zero and returns this pointer identity
enum branch: getBase(1,TYPE_UINT) pointee, off reset to 0
relative dispatch: relOff=16 drills the parent's total field via plain recursion
relOff==0 && offset!=0: parent pointer returned, accumulators untouched (type.cc:2669-2670)
relOff=24 reaches parent size: NULL before interning or mutating off
deferral: plain body invoked on the rel pointer itself, par=this observes the rel identity
relOff=6 lands in the parent hole: recursive plain NULL passes through with no fallback (type.cc:2671)
off==ptrto getSize leaves the deferral guard and takes the parent-relative path
routing discrimination: scalar ptrto yields NULL on the plain path but the first field through the rel path
